segments.text: Linda, many, many congratulations.
First things first, can you tell us how you have celebrated
becoming a Wimbledon champion over the past 30 hours or so?
There was definitely some champagne, you know, obviously.
Some of this, some of that.
I had a great time with my team, with my friends, with my family,
and a lot of stress-free time.
Any Czech beer?
Not yet, no. In 24 hours, I hope so.
It's on the way. Listen, you and Carolina produced the most extraordinary performance on court yesterday,
and then both came up with two brilliant speeches.
How difficult was it for you to play such a close friend in such a big final?
It's never easy to play someone you know very well.
it's always really tough to play against such a friend of mine you know we have
spent a lot of time together especially at the Olympics we really got to know
each other very well so it was not easy but you know she was an open and just
like any other unfortunately. Can I just check that you are good friends again as
opposed to ex-friends? I mean we haven't talked since then so I hope that we
will still make it, you know, make up. I think you will. Now listen, you have joined a great
list of Czech champions, Martina Navratilova and Petra Kvideva amongst them who were in
the royal box yesterday. How proud are you to be part of such a special group? Very
proud, especially proud of our country. We have a lot of Grand Slam champions and I'm
so proud of myself as well to, you know, kind of call myself one of them as well.
And you made a very touching reference to your mother after the match yesterday. A couple of
years ago, she used the adjective unflappable to describe you. Has that been the key ingredient
in winning that match yesterday and indeed throughout your career? I think she was the
main ingredient. Like I said in the speech, I would not be there without any of my parents
or without my team and without everyone supporting me in my journey. So it was a mix of everybody.
Well I'm sure everybody will appreciate those sentiments. And just one final word. You have
so many interests aside from tennis you care about humanity the environment animal rights
how important is that aspect of your life to you along with your tennis it's very important it's
very close and dear to me and my heart i have always been kind of brought up that way so i feel
like i can definitely use my platform to do some great things off court as well you're doing great
things on court and off court. Many congratulations, Linda, and if I could now ask Debbie Jevons
to come up. You were looking at the Venus rosewater dish very closely after your win yesterday.
Here's a replica trophy you can grab forever.
Ladies and gentlemen, our 2026 Ladies Singles Champion, Linda Noskova.
